newsitem.title: UK: BP shares surge on results, buy-back plans.
newsitem.headline: BP shares surge on results, buy-back plans.

text.p: Shares in oil company British Petroleum surged on Tuesday after the company released second quarter earnings above analysts forecasts and unexpectedly revealed plans to buy-back shares.
BP jumped 17p to 839p after being up 6-1/2p ahead of the news.

The company said second quarter replacement cost net profit, excluding exceptional items came to 740 million stg compared with a consensus estimate of 661 million stg. A dividend of 5.5p per share was if anything, better than average expectations, dealers said.
"Headline earnings overshot our expectations and the dividend was better than the consensus," one trader said.
The shares later extended gains and broke the previous all-time high to be trading at 848p by 1105 GMT.
Peter Hitchens, oil analyst at Williams de Broe, described the results as "a brilliant set of numbers" adding they would set a trend for the rest of the sector and possibly prompt earnings upgrades.
"I think we are going to see better-than-expected results across the board," Hitchens said. "U.S. and European oil majors have also been turning in strong numbers."
Meanwhile, BP unexpectedly announced it would seek shareholder approval to buy back shares from "time to time" now that the company's cash flow and balance sheet were robust.
"Share buy back plans have always been rumoured since BP did incredibly well at bringing its debt under control," Hitchens commented. "But it still came as a surprise."
